# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.

package net.officefloor.hq.app.claim;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.math.RoundingMode;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.temporal.ChronoUnit;

/**
 * What makes an overdue claim's late charge: the sheet's late percent (two decimals) and its today; a claim is due
 * by the due-by fixed when it was added. The charge is never bound by a statement: it follows the sheet's today.
 * It also carries the sheet's policy date, which decides how a claim's live figures round.
 */
public record Late(BigDecimal pct, LocalDate today, LocalDate policy) {

    /**
     * How the claim's live figures round: half up when it rounds on a date (its own, or for a correction the date of
     * the claim it corrects) before the policy date, half to even on or after it.
     */
    public RoundingMode rounding(Claim claim) {
        return LocalDate.parse(claim.roundsOn()).isBefore(policy) ? RoundingMode.HALF_UP : RoundingMode.HALF_EVEN;
    }

    /** Whether the claim is overdue: OPEN or PENDING with its due-by (fixed when it was added) before the sheet's today. */
    public boolean overdue(Claim claim) {
        return (claim.status() == ClaimStatus.OPEN || claim.status() == ClaimStatus.PENDING) && LocalDate.parse(claim.dueBy()).isBefore(today);
    }

    /**
     * The claim's late charge on its figure: the late percent of the figure for every full 30 days it is overdue,
     * rounded in hundredths by the claim's {@link #rounding}; 0.00 when it is not overdue, and always for a correction.
     */
    public BigDecimal charge(Claim claim, BigDecimal figure) {
        if (figure == null || claim.correction() || !overdue(claim)) {
            return BigDecimal.ZERO.setScale(2);
        }
        long days = ChronoUnit.DAYS.between(LocalDate.parse(claim.dueBy()), today);
        return figure.multiply(pct).multiply(BigDecimal.valueOf(days / 30)).movePointLeft(2).setScale(2,
                rounding(claim));
    }
}
package net.officefloor.hq.app.claim;

import net.officefloor.hq.app.Audit;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.period.Periods;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.person.Person;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.rollup.Rollup;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.setting.Settings;
import net.officefloor.plugin.variable.Val;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;

public class BuildClaim {
    public void build(@PathVariable("sheet") String sheet, @RequestParam("user") String user, @Val Person person,
            @Val ClaimInput input, Claims claims, Periods periods, Settings settings, Audit audit, Rollup rollup)
            throws InvalidClaimException {
        if (periods.closedOn(sheet, input.date())) {
            throw new InvalidClaimException("A claim may not be dated inside a closed period");
        }
        if (person.retiredBefore(input.date())) {
            throw new InvalidClaimException("A claim may not be dated after the person's retirement date");
        }
        input.checkCorrects(sheet, person.id(), claims);
        Rollup.Snapshot before = rollup.take(sheet);
        // The due-by is fixed now, from the terms of the person's grade in force on the claim's date.
        claims.add(sheet, person.id(), input, input.date().plusDays(settings.terms(sheet, person.gradeOn(input.date()))));
        audit.record("CLAIM_ADDED sheet=" + sheet + " by=" + user + " " + input.auditFields(person.name()));
        rollup.record(sheet, user, before);
    }
}

Each claim now shows its status log, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it works**
- **Storage:** a new table, added in migration `V25__claim_log.sql`, keeps one line per status a claim has had. Each line holds the status, the user, the sheet's today at the time, and the due already formatted (two decimals, or `n/a` when the grade has no rate).
- **Writing lines:** a new `ClaimLog` service (`claim/ClaimLog.java`) re-reads the claim after each change, computes its due the same way the screen does, and writes the line. It's called in two places:
  - `BuildClaim`, for the DRAFT line when a claim is added. Quick-add goes through this too. To support it, `Claims.add` now returns the new claim's id.
  - `ClaimStatusChanger`, after every status change, including bulk open. A settle or approve writes its line after the due is fixed, so the line shows the settled figure.
- **Reading lines:** the `Claim` record has a new `log` field. `Claims.list` and `Claims.find` load the lines oldest first and attach them, so they arrive with the existing claims response.
- **Screen:** each claim row lists the lines as `claim-log-line` items, e.g. `SETTLED by vic on 2026-03-11 due=4.00`.

**Things to know**
- Claims that existed before this change start with an empty log. Nothing records who made their earlier changes or when, so I didn't make up lines for them.
- A refused change writes no line, because the line is written only after the status update succeeds.
- Editing a draft and reassigning a claim don't add lines, since neither changes the status. The DRAFT line keeps the due from when the claim was added, which is what the test expects.
